- **Stable release:** AutoCert 1.0.0.0 is now a regular release.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Status after restart:** Resolved a stale restart message. Show Certificate Active when Jellyfin reports HTTPS listening, no restart is pending, certificate settings match, and the AutoCert PFX is valid.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Error visibility:** Preserve staging messages and renewal failures.

## ✨ New Features

- **GoDaddy authentication:** Use a classic API key and secret alongside the existing GoDaddy PAT, Cloudflare, and DigitalOcean options.
- **HTTPS management:** DNS verification, automatic renewal, password-protected PFX creation, password rotation, Jellyfin HTTPS configuration updates, optional restart, and rollback.

versions.changelog:
## Español

### 3.0.4 — Fechas, búsqueda, guardado y migración

- Corrige el cierre de Jellyfin Android TV al abrir bibliotecas: el caché de consultas descartaba `DateTimeKind.Utc` al bufferizar y el cliente recibía fechas sin zona horaria, que sustituía por su valor mínimo y hacían fallar la conversión. Las columnas de fecha se bufferizan como UTC y el lector restaura el `Kind` como segunda barrera.
- Nueva migración que normaliza fechas no finitas o mínimas ya guardadas en `BaseItems`, y normalización de los centinelas `DateTime` y `DateTimeOffset` antes de escribir.
- La búsqueda deja de distinguir mayúsculas y minúsculas e incluye título visible, título original y título para ordenar, con índice trigram sobre `SortName`.
- Corrige el error 500 al abrir la ficha de un artista o persona: las filas duplicadas se resuelven con una actualización sin cambios sobre la clave primaria en lugar de `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, que informaba 0 filas y EF Core trataba como conflicto de concurrencia.
- Corrige la migración SQLite → PostgreSQL: se conserva el historial de rutinas de código ya aplicadas, identificadas por el nombre de la migración. Sin él, Jellyfin volvía a ejecutar rutinas que esperan `library.db` y el arranque fallaba con `no such table: TypedBaseItems` (#9).
- El proveedor fija `QuerySplittingBehavior` en `SingleQuery`, igual que el proveedor SQLite, y deja de llenar el log con `MultipleCollectionIncludeWarning`.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.4 — Dates, search, saving, and migration

- Fixes Jellyfin Android TV crashing when a library is opened: the query cache dropped `DateTimeKind.Utc` while buffering, so the client received dates without a time zone, replaced them with its minimum value, and failed converting it. Date columns are buffered as UTC and the reader restores the `Kind` as a second safeguard.
- New migration that normalizes non-finite or minimum dates already stored in `BaseItems`, plus normalization of `DateTime` and `DateTimeOffset` sentinels before writing.
- Search is no longer case-sensitive and now covers display, original, and sort titles, with a trigram index on `SortName`.
- Fixes the 500 returned when opening an artist or person page: duplicate rows are resolved with a no-op update on the primary key instead of `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, which reported zero affected rows and EF Core treated as a concurrency conflict.
- Fixes the SQLite → PostgreSQL migration: the history of code migrations already applied is preserved, matched by migration name. Without it, Jellyfin re-ran routines that expect `library.db` and startup failed with `no such table: TypedBaseItems` (#9).
- The provider pins `QuerySplittingBehavior` to `SingleQuery`, matching Jellyfin's SQLite provider, and stops flooding the log with `MultipleCollectionIncludeWarning`.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.3 — Integraciones privadas, mantenimiento y estabilidad

- Nuevo host seguro para esquemas privados de plugins: registro, migraciones aisladas y acceso sin exponer credenciales ni el esquema `public` de Jellyfin.
- Nueva pestaña **Integraciones** para revisar esquemas registrados, consultar una muestra limitada de datos, ver métricas por tabla y administrar `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` y `REINDEX` por esquema.
- Las tareas programadas mantienen `public` y solo los esquemas privados autorizados por el administrador.
- Health incorpora métricas de presión de buffers, bloques leídos, uso temporal y WAL para diagnosticar consultas lentas.
- Estado actual detecta el motor activo sin esperar la validación SQLite; esta continúa en segundo plano y se vuelve a comprobar antes de revertir.
- Se refuerza el aislamiento de identificadores en operaciones de exploración y mantenimiento de esquemas privados.
- Documentación actualizada en español e inglés, incluida la integración para desarrolladores, exportación SQLite segura y orientación para Docker.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.3 — Private integrations, maintenance, and stability

- New secure host for private plugin schemas: registration, isolated migrations, and storage without exposing credentials or Jellyfin's `public` schema.
- New **Integrations** tab to review registered schemas, inspect a bounded data sample, view per-table metrics, and manage `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM (ANALYZE)`, and `REINDEX` per schema.
- Scheduled tasks maintain `public` and only private schemas explicitly enabled by an administrator.
- Health adds buffer-pressure, blocks-read, temporary-I/O, and WAL metrics for slow-query diagnosis.
- Current status detects the active engine without waiting for SQLite validation; validation continues in the background and is checked again before rollback.
- Strengthens identifier isolation in private-schema exploration and maintenance operations.
- Updated Spanish and English documentation, including developer integration, safe SQLite export, and Docker guidance.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.2 — Estabilidad, integridad y exportación segura

- Corrige la normalización de `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset` y arreglos antes de escribir en PostgreSQL, evitando errores de Npgsql por `Kind` incompatible.
- Las escrituras concurrentes de `UserData` y las actualizaciones completas de elementos usan upserts atómicos para reducir conflictos durante actualizaciones bajo demanda.
- La activación de PostgreSQL valida la conexión antes de modificar `database.xml`.
- Se elimina la restauración automática de backups y la restauración manual no reemplaza objetos existentes por defecto.
- Las consultas concurrentes idénticas de inicio se consolidan mientras se llena la caché.
- La exportación PostgreSQL → SQLite crea y valida un `library.db` SQLite real; evita el archivo inválido que impedía iniciar Jellyfin.
- La exportación ya no copia ni marca a ciegas el historial de migraciones.

Verificado con Build Release, pruebas unitarias e integración real contra PostgreSQL. Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+ y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.2 — Stability, integrity and safe export

- Fixes normalization of `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, and arrays before PostgreSQL writes, avoiding Npgsql errors caused by incompatible `Kind` values.
- Concurrent `UserData` writes and full item updates use atomic upserts to reduce conflicts during on-demand updates.
- PostgreSQL activation validates the connection before changing `database.xml`.
- Automatic backup restore was removed, and manual restore no longer replaces existing objects by default.
- Identical concurrent home-screen queries are coalesced while the cache is populated.
- PostgreSQL → SQLite export creates and validates a real SQLite `library.db`, preventing the invalid file that stopped Jellyfin from starting.
- Export no longer blindly marks or copies migration history.

Verified with a Release build, unit tests, and real PostgreSQL integration tests. Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+, and .NET 10.

3.0.1 - Correccion de la integracion con JellyTrend

- Fix: el esquema jellytrend no creaba la tabla donde el motor de JellyTrend guarda el perfil de gustos aprendido (user_affinity), asi que ese perfil no quedaba almacenado. El esquema se crea ahora completo (version 4).
- El esquema se comprueba al arrancar: en una instalacion 3.0.0 la tabla que faltaba se crea sola. No hay que recrear el esquema ni reinstalar nada.
- Docs: la seccion de integracion con JellyTrend documenta las dos piezas del contrato: almacen de datos en el esquema jellytrend (fuera de public, para no colarse en las exportaciones a SQLite) y acelerador de consultas con SQL nativo en las recomendaciones (4-10x en bibliotecas grandes).

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x. Para Jellyfin 10.11.x usa la version 2.0.1.

- Opciones avanzadas funcionales: tamano de pool, sentencias preparadas y tiempo de espera se validan, se guardan, se reflejan en el estado actual y se aplican al proveedor.

- Exportacion a SQLite mas robusta: claves primarias verbatim, diagnostico de constraint, limpieza de filas huerfanas y library.db minimo valido para el arranque.

Verificacion

- Auditor de esquema contra el modelo EF del servidor.

Documentacion

name: Marquee Companion [✓]
description:
Adds server-side library filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), opt-in recovery of missing release dates from file names or date added, authenticated Apple Watch media grants, and server-stored profile PINs. - Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.

  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.

  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a

  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into

  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.

  only a short-lived direct HTTPS media URL, safe headers, and its expiry. The executable is
  not packaged with the plugin.

- Adds an optional plugin-managed resolver binary. An administrator selects a source — an
  exact pinned release, or the newest stable or nightly build — and the plugin fetches only
  official yt-dlp GitHub release assets, verifying each download against that release's
  published SHA-256 manifest before it is made executable. Both endpoints require elevation,
  and binaries are stored outside the plugin's version-stamped directory so they survive
  plugin updates. A failed process start no longer disables the resolver until the server
  restarts when the executable behind it has changed.
- A managed resolver now also installs the JavaScript runtime yt-dlp needs (Deno), verified
  against its published SHA-256 checksum and extracted from the release archive, and points
  yt-dlp at it. Without a runtime yt-dlp reports YouTube extraction as deprecated and some
  formats may be missing. It is fetched only when absent, and there is nothing to configure.
  Hosts with no published runtime — musl/Alpine — are reported plainly rather than silently
  degraded. The resolve timeout moves from 10 to 30 seconds to accommodate runtime start-up
  and signature deciphering; a timeout would otherwise surface as a silently missing trailer.
- Adds an optional daily scheduled task that installs the newest build on the tracked
  channel. It is visible and controllable under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks, does nothing
  unless a tracking source has automatic updates enabled, and never advances a pinned
  version. The newest three builds per channel are retained so a bad build can be rolled
  back by pinning the previous one, without a download.

They are now recognised as virtual and ignored, so your Trakt recommendations come through
- An empty "Trakt for you" is no longer sticky: a null or empty result is cached only briefly, so once the server has your picks they appear on the next open instead of being held behind a stale empty view
- A rate-limited or unreachable Trakt is retried with a backoff (honouring the server's Retry-After) instead of being re-hit on every tab load, and the same account open on two devices now shares one fetch instead of firing two
- An unlinked user no longer sees a "Trakt for you" tab that only shows a not-linked message; the tab appears once you are linked, and "Trakt trending" (which needs no login) is always available

## Developer

## Features
- Replace a library song's audio with a different YouTube upload from the Download tab; it keeps the song's file, tags, cover and playlist places.
- Choosing an album already in the library on the Import tab takes that album's cover.
- Imports join existing artist and album folders whose names differ only in case, punctuation or year, and take that album's name and year.

## Features
- Republishes 12.2.3.0, whose download did not match its checksum and could not install.

## Features
- Import Spotify playlists exported with Exportify, one playlist as CSV or all of them as a ZIP.
- Spotify imports embed Spotify's album cover and fill in the genre from Apple Music.
- Playlist tracks with an ISRC are matched to their official YouTube upload by it first.
- Generate a cover with the wand button on the Import tab; choose its text, order and colors in Settings → Album Art.
- Composer credits are stored as separate composers.
- Live, remix, cover, acoustic and instrumental versions are never matched unless the song's title names that version.

## Features
- When Apple Music has no cover, the album cover from the official YouTube Music track is used.
- Re-pitched, sped-up, 8D and nightcore uploads are never matched.
- Artists YouTube Music credits in another alphabet (such as Cyrillic) are matched by album or exact length.
- Re-importing a playlist removes queued or failed songs your library now has.

## Features
- YouTube matches must contain the song title, so another song by the same artist with a similar length is never downloaded instead.
- Importing rescans only the imported songs' folders instead of the whole library.

## Features
- Look up each download on Apple Music to fill in its title, album, album artist, year, track number and genre (Settings, on by default).
- Embed the album cover from Apple Music in downloaded files (Settings, on by default).
- Upload your own cover art on the Import tab, for one file or all selected files.
- Songs already in your library are marked Already in your library on the Import tab.
- Joint artist credits are stored as separate artists, and new imports reuse the library's spelling of an artist.
- Playlist imports use the album's release date for its year.
- Playlist tracks the regular YouTube search cannot match are looked up in YouTube Music's song results.

## Features
- Change the YouTube link of any queued track from its queue row, keeping its details and playlist.
- Better matching for classical tracks, and uploads by other performers are no longer picked.
- Classical tracks already in your library are recognized even when tagged with only the movement name (or only the full work title), so they are not downloaded again.

## Features
- Preview downloaded tracks on the Import tab before importing them.
- Genres are capitalized, split into separate genres, and standardized (for example alt-pop becomes Alternative and Pop).

## Features
- Import Apple Music playlists (text or XML export) and whole library exports; each track is matched to a YouTube upload at download time.
- Imported playlists become private Jellyfin playlists for a chosen user, filled as songs reach the library, appended to and re-ordered when one of the same name exists.
- Import cleanup groups album editions (Deluxe, Remastered, Bonus Track…), moves feat. artists into tags, skips songs already in the library or queue, and upgrades library singles to the album version.
- Public read-only queue page at /YouTube/Queue for signed-in users.
- yt-dlp and the Deno runtime it needs for YouTube are downloaded automatically, yt-dlp is kept up to date, and downloads YouTube temporarily refuses are retried.
